_**Cowboy Carter**_ (stylized in [all caps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_caps "All caps"); also referred to as _**Act II: Cowboy Carter**_) is the eighth studio album by American singer and songwriter [Beyoncé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyonc%C3%A9 "Beyoncé"). It was released on March 29, 2024, by [Parkwood Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parkwood_Entertainment "Parkwood Entertainment") and [Columbia Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Records "Columbia Records"). A [concept album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concept_album "Concept album"), _Cowboy Carter_ is the second of a planned trilogy of albums, following _[Renaissance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renaissance_\(Beyonc%C3%A9_album\) "Renaissance \(Beyoncé album\)")_ (2022). Beyoncé conceived the album as a journey through a reinvention of [Americana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Americana "Americana"), spotlighting the overlooked contributions of Black pioneers to [American musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_history_of_the_United_States "Music history of the United States") and [cultural history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culture_of_the_United_States "Culture of the United States").
A genre-blending album rooted in [country music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music"), _Cowboy Carter_ is influenced by Beyoncé's upbringing in [Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas "Texas"), incorporating eclectic styles of [music of the Southern United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_of_the_Southern_United_States "Music of the Southern United States"). Conceptually, the album is presented as a radio broadcast, with country singers [Dolly Parton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolly_Parton "Dolly Parton"), [Linda Martell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linda_Martell "Linda Martell"), and [Willie Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson "Willie Nelson") acting as disc jockeys. The album's songs feature rising Black country artists such as [Shaboozey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaboozey "Shaboozey"), [Tanner Adell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanner_Adell "Tanner Adell"), [Brittney Spencer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brittney_Spencer "Brittney Spencer"), [Tiera Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiera_Kennedy "Tiera Kennedy"), [Reyna Roberts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reyna_Roberts "Reyna Roberts"), and [Willie Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Jones_\(country_singer\) "Willie Jones \(country singer\)"). The music is driven by a range of [acoustic instruments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acoustic_instruments "Acoustic instruments") played by musicians including [Stevie Wonder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stevie_Wonder "Stevie Wonder"), [Paul McCartney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_McCartney "Paul McCartney"), and [Nile Rodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nile_Rodgers "Nile Rodgers"), among others.
_Cowboy Carter_ was met with universal acclaim and appeared on multiple year-end lists; critics stated that the album's genre experimentation, expansive scope and eclectic references aided an ambitious reimagining of Americana and country through the lens of their Black roots. At the [67th Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Grammy_Awards "67th Grammy Awards"), Beyoncé became the first Black woman in 25 years to win [Album of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year") and the first Black artist to win [Best Country Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Country_Album "Best Country Album"); the album's third single, "[II Most Wanted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/II_Most_Wanted "II Most Wanted")", won [Best Country Duo/Group Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Country_Duo/Group_Performance "Best Country Duo/Group Performance"). The album increased the listenership of country music, drove cultural conversations on Black musicians' place within the genre, boosted the careers of rising country artists, and increased the popularity of [Western wear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_wear "Western wear") and [culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_lifestyle "Western lifestyle").
_Cowboy Carter_ debuted at number one in several countries and broke multiple chart and streaming records. In the United States, it topped the [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200") and was Beyoncé's first to top the [Top Country Albums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top_Country_Albums "Top Country Albums") chart, selling 407,000 [album-equivalent units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Album-equivalent_unit "Album-equivalent unit"). The album was supported by three singles, "[Texas Hold 'Em](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Hold_'Em_\(song\) "Texas Hold 'Em \(song\)")", "[16 Carriages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/16_Carriages "16 Carriages")", and "II Most Wanted", with the first becoming Beyoncé's ninth US number-one single and the first country song by a Black woman to top the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") and [Hot Country Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Country_Songs "Hot Country Songs") charts. To support the album, Beyoncé embarked on the [Cowboy Carter Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter_Tour "Cowboy Carter Tour") from April 28 to July 26, 2025.
## Background and development
Beyoncé was born and raised in [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston "Houston"), where the city's [cowboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy "Cowboy") heritage and [country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") and [zydeco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zydeco "Zydeco") music played a role in her upbringing.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Thorpe-BBC-4)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-5) She listened to country music from an early age, particularly from her paternal grandfather, and her family attended the [Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Livestock_Show_and_Rodeo "Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo") every year in [western clothing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_clothing "Western clothing").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-6) She performed at the Rodeo four times between 2001 and 2007, and has continued to celebrate her country and [Southern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culture_of_the_Southern_United_States "Culture of the Southern United States") roots throughout her career.[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-12)
> I grew up going to the [Houston rodeo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Livestock_Show_and_Rodeo "Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo") every year. It was this amazing, diverse and multicultural experience where there was something for every member of the family, including great performances, [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston "Houston")-style fried [Snickers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snickers "Snickers"), and fried turkey legs. One of my inspirations came from the overlooked history of the American [Black cowboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_cowboy "Black cowboy"). Many of them were originally called cowhands, who experienced great discrimination and were often forced to work with the worst, most temperamental horses. They took their talents and formed the Soul Circuit. Through time, these Black rodeos showcased incredible performers and helped us reclaim our place in [western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_lifestyle "Western lifestyle") history and culture.
— Beyoncé to _[Harper's Bazaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harper's_Bazaar "Harper's Bazaar")_ in 2021[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-HB-13)
Beyoncé first released an original country song in 2016: the track "[Daddy Lessons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daddy_Lessons "Daddy Lessons")" on her sixth studio album, _[Lemonade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lemonade_\(album\) "Lemonade \(album\)")_.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-14) Beyoncé, together with [the Chicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Chicks "The Chicks") (who had previously covered the song), performed the track at the [50th Annual Country Music Association Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/50th_Annual_Country_Music_Association_Awards "50th Annual Country Music Association Awards") on November 2, 2016. The performance was largely praised by critics and gave the [Country Music Association Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_Music_Association_Awards "Country Music Association Awards") their highest viewership in history; however, it was also met with backlash, with some country music fans criticizing Beyoncé's attendance and claiming she did not belong in the genre. The [Country Music Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_Music_Association "Country Music Association") deleted all promotional posts about Beyoncé's performance, which was seen by some observers as succumbing to the pressure from conservative and racist viewers.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-15)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-16) In December 2016, [The Recording Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Recording_Academy "The Recording Academy")'s country music committee rejected "Daddy Lessons" for consideration for a [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award"), with publications reporting that the song was not seen as being "country enough".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-17)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-18)
This experience led to the creation of _Cowboy Carter_. Beyoncé explained how it was made clear to her that she was not welcome in the country music space, which encouraged her to explore the musical history of the genre rather than letting the critics force her out of it. She delved into the history of country music and [Western culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_lifestyle "Western lifestyle") and researched its African-American roots. She studied "our rich musical archive" and learned from educators who had long advocated for a re-education on the Black roots of country music. She also read that, historically, half of cowboys were Black, which made her realize how much of the Black, brown, and Native cowboy stories are missing in American history.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-19) This was the inspiration for her 2021 "[Ivy Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivy_Park "Ivy Park") Rodeo" clothing collection.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-HB-13) Following this research, Beyoncé conceived _Cowboy Carter_ as a journey through a reinvention of Americana, in which she redefines its boundaries and spotlights overlooked contributions of African Americans to diverse musical genres, Southern and Western culture, and American history.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Beyonc%C3%A9_Releases_Cowboy_Carter-20) Collaborator [Rhiannon Giddens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhiannon_Giddens "Rhiannon Giddens") said Beyoncé did not intend to create a typical [crossover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crossover_music "Crossover music") country album, but instead wanted to explore her family's roots through music.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-21)
_Cowboy Carter_ was over five years in the making. Beyoncé began to write the album in 2019, then recorded during the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), which she described as her most creative period.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-22) The album forms "Act II" of a trilogy project that Beyoncé recorded during this period.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-23) The first act, _[Renaissance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renaissance_\(Beyonc%C3%A9_album\) "Renaissance \(Beyoncé album\)")_ (2022), is primarily a [house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_music "House music") and [disco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disco "Disco") record highlighting and celebrating the Black progenitors of [dance music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance_music "Dance music"), leading some to believe that each album of the trilogy would aim to explore the Black roots of a different musical genre.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Thorpe-BBC-4) _Cowboy Carter_ was originally intended to be released before _Renaissance_ , but Beyoncé changed the order in response to the pandemic.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Paul-2024-24) Between 2020 and 2024, [Dolly Parton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolly_Parton "Dolly Parton") often said that she would like Beyoncé to cover her song "[Jolene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jolene "Jolene")".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-25)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-26)
While working on the album, she reached out to [Miley Cyrus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miley_Cyrus "Miley Cyrus") to collaborate with her on _Cowboy Carter_. Cyrus presented her with "[Easy Lover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easy_Lover_\(Miley_Cyrus_song\) "Easy Lover \(Miley Cyrus song\)")" and "Shotgun Rider", and Beyoncé chose the latter, renaming it "[II Most Wanted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/II_Most_Wanted "II Most Wanted")".[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-27)
## Composition
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/76/Willie_Nelson_in_Redmond%2C_Washington_2008.jpg/250px-Willie_Nelson_in_Redmond%2C_Washington_2008.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Willie_Nelson_in_Redmond,_Washington_2008.jpg)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/49/Stevie_Wonder_performs_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Stevie_Wonder_performs_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Stevie_Wonder_performs_\(cropped\).jpg)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c5/Nile_Rodgers_Coachella18W1-186_%2841157644435%29_%28cropped%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Nile_Rodgers_Coachella18W1-186_%2841157644435%29_%28cropped%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nile_Rodgers_Coachella18W1-186_\(41157644435\)_\(cropped\)_\(cropped\).jpg)
In addition to up-and-coming country artists, various established musicians contributed to _Cowboy Carter_ , including [Willie Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson "Willie Nelson"), [Stevie Wonder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stevie_Wonder "Stevie Wonder") and [Nile Rodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nile_Rodgers "Nile Rodgers").
> The joy of creating music is that there are no rules. The more I see the world evolving the more I felt a deeper connection to purity. With [artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence "Artificial intelligence") and digital filters and programming, I wanted to go back to real instruments, and I used very old ones. I didn't want some layers of instruments like strings, especially guitars, and [organs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_\(music\) "Organ \(music\)") perfectly in tune. I kept some songs raw and leaned into [folk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_music "Folk music"). All the sounds were so organic and human, everyday things like the wind, snaps and even the sound of birds and chickens, the sounds of nature.
— Beyoncé on _Cowboy Carter_[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-28)
Beyoncé recorded around 100 songs for the album.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Paul-2024-24) Each song is its own reimagined version of a [Western film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_film "Western film"),[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-29) including _[Five Fingers for Marseilles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Five_Fingers_for_Marseilles "Five Fingers for Marseilles")_ (2017), _[Urban Cowboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_Cowboy "Urban Cowboy")_ (1980), _[The Hateful Eight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hateful_Eight "The Hateful Eight")_ (2015), _[Space Cowboys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Cowboys "Space Cowboys")_ (2000), _[The Harder They Fall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Harder_They_Fall_\(2021_film\) "The Harder They Fall \(2021 film\)")_ (2021), _[Killers of the Flower Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killers_of_the_Flower_Moon "Killers of the Flower Moon")_ (2023), _[Thelma& Louise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thelma_&_Louise "Thelma & Louise")_ (1991) and _[O Brother, Where Art Thou?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/O_Brother,_Where_Art_Thou%3F "O Brother, Where Art Thou?")_ (2000).[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Beyonc%C3%A9_Releases_Cowboy_Carter-20)
Rooted in [country music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music"),[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-30) _Cowboy Carter_ is a genre-spanning album that blends various styles of [American roots music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_roots_music "American roots music"), in particular that of the [American South](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_South "American South").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-31)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-32) Publications categorized it as [country pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_pop "Country pop"),[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-33) country,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-34) [outlaw country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outlaw_country "Outlaw country"),[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Moran-2024-35) [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music"),[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-xgau-36) [western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_music_\(North_America\) "Western music \(North America\)"), [country-soul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country-soul "Country-soul"), [blues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blues "Blues"), [hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip-hop "Hip-hop"), [R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_R&B "Contemporary R&B"),[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-thetimes-37) and [Americana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Americana_music "Americana music"),[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Slant-38) It further explores elements of [folk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_music "Folk music"), and various other styles that Beyoncé listened to when growing up in Texas, including [zydeco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zydeco "Zydeco"), [rock and roll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_roll "Rock and roll"), [psychedelic soul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychedelic_soul "Psychedelic soul"), [rhythm and blues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythm_and_blues "Rhythm and blues"), [funk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funk "Funk"), [gospel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gospel_music "Gospel music"), [bluegrass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bluegrass_music "Bluegrass music"), [opera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opera "Opera"), [Southern hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_hip-hop "Southern hip-hop"), [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music"), [honky-tonk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honky-tonk "Honky-tonk"), and [go-go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Go-go "Go-go").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-TheGuardian-39)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-40)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-41) The album also fuses in more contemporary and international musical styles, such as [house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_music "House music"), [Jersey club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jersey_club "Jersey club"), [flamenco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flamenco "Flamenco"), [funk carioca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funk_carioca "Funk carioca"), [fado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fado "Fado") and [Irish folk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_folk "Irish folk").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Moran-2024-35)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-42) Beyoncé's experimentation with musical styles on _Cowboy Carter_ aims to break down the limitations placed on genre-based music, in the service of redefining the boundaries of Americana.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Beyonc%C3%A9_Releases_Cowboy_Carter-20)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-43) The album's genre experimentation received significant discussion in the media, with publications describing the album as "[genre-busting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genre-busting "Genre-busting")", "genre-defying", "genre-bending" and "genre-blending".[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-44)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-PBSNewsHour-45)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-46)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-47) Music critics differed in their classification of the album: some simply defined it as "country" or "country-and-Western",[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Contreras-2024-48)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Nanji-2024-49) while others opined that the album is not a country album _per se_ but uses country signifiers to explore various genres.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Mframa-50)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-51)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-52) Beyoncé herself said about _Cowboy Carter_ : "This ain't a Country album. This is a 'Beyoncé' album." _[USA Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Today "USA Today")_ 's Kofi Mframa said this description was a "resounding testament to Beyoncé's long history of refusal to adhere to the traditional confines of genre".[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Mframa-50)
The album is presented as a broadcast by a fictional Texas radio station, with country singers Dolly Parton, [Linda Martell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linda_Martell "Linda Martell") and [Willie Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson "Willie Nelson") acting as radio DJs.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Kreps-2024-53) The album features rising country artists [Tanner Adell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanner_Adell "Tanner Adell"), [Brittney Spencer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brittney_Spencer "Brittney Spencer"), [Tiera Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiera_Kennedy "Tiera Kennedy"), [Reyna Roberts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reyna_Roberts "Reyna Roberts"), [Shaboozey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaboozey "Shaboozey") and [Willie Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Jones_\(country_singer\) "Willie Jones \(country singer\)").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Beyonc%C3%A9_Releases_Cowboy_Carter-20) The album is cyclical, with the final note looping seamlessly into the beginning of the first track (which begins "Nothing really ends") in the same manner as James Joyce's _[Finnegans Wake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finnegans_Wake "Finnegans Wake")_ (1939), according to _[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Washington_Post "The Washington Post")_ 's Shane O'Neill.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-54) The album features a range of [acoustic instruments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acoustic_instruments "Acoustic instruments") played by musicians including [Stevie Wonder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stevie_Wonder "Stevie Wonder") on harmonica, [Paul McCartney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_McCartney "Paul McCartney") and [Nile Rodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nile_Rodgers "Nile Rodgers") on guitar, and [Rhiannon Giddens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhiannon_Giddens "Rhiannon Giddens") on banjo.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-55)
## Promotion and release
### Lead singles
Main articles: [Texas Hold 'Em (song)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Hold_'Em_\(song\) "Texas Hold 'Em \(song\)") and [16 Carriages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/16_Carriages "16 Carriages")
On February 11, 2024, during [Super Bowl LVIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII "Super Bowl LVIII"), [Verizon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verizon "Verizon") aired a [commercial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_commercials "Super Bowl commercials") starring Beyoncé entitled "Can't B Broken", in which she tried to "break the Internet" through increasingly outlandish means, such as releasing a [jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jazz "Jazz") saxophone record, performing on top of [Sphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sphere_\(venue\) "Sphere \(venue\)") in Las Vegas, building an [artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence "Artificial intelligence") (AI) version of herself, launching a collection of [Barbie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbie "Barbie")-like dolls dubbed "BarBey", announcing her candidacy for a fictional political position, and flying into space for a performance. After all of the ideas proved unsuccessful, Beyoncé concluded the commercial by remarking: "Okay, they ready. Drop the new music".[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-56)
After the commercial aired, Beyoncé released a teaser video for _Act II_ on [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-57) Directed by British artist and filmmaker [Nadia Lee Cohen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadia_Lee_Cohen "Nadia Lee Cohen"), the video pays homage to _[Paris, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris,_Texas_\(film\) "Paris, Texas \(film\)")_ (1984), references [border blasters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Border_blaster "Border blaster") and features [Chuck Berry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Berry "Chuck Berry")'s 1955 track "[Maybellene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maybellene "Maybellene")".[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-58)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-59) The same day, the singer's official website was updated to announce her eighth studio album, with the placeholder name _Act II_ , scheduled for release on March 29.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-60) Subsequently, the album's two lead singles, "[Texas Hold 'Em](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Hold_'Em_\(song\) "Texas Hold 'Em \(song\)")" and "[16 Carriages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/16_Carriages "16 Carriages")", were simultaneously made available for digital download and streaming.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-61)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-62) On March 12, Beyoncé announced the album would be titled _Cowboy Carter_[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-63) via a teaser poster of a [western saddle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_saddle "Western saddle") with a [sash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sash "Sash").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-64) She also listed album merchandise, including limited-edition CDs with a [bonus track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonus_track "Bonus track"), [T-shirts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T-shirts "T-shirts"), and [vinyl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phonograph_record "Phonograph record") variants in red, white, blue, and standard black.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-65)
### Album release
On March 19, 2024, Beyoncé revealed the album cover via Instagram, and said there would be "surprises" and collaborations on the album.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-pitchfork1-66) On March 20, she revealed a limited edition exclusive cover, wearing a sash that reads "act ii BEYINCÉ", referencing the generational family surname of her mother, [Tina Knowles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tina_Knowles "Tina Knowles").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-67)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-68) Taglines and [film stills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_stills "Film stills") for the album were projected onto various museums in New York City.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-69) One was an unauthorized projection onto the [Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solomon_R._Guggenheim_Museum "Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum"), which responded good-naturedly by posting [Franz Marc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franz_Marc "Franz Marc")'s 1910 painting _Three Horses Drinking_ with the caption "This ain't Texas" in reference to "Texas Hold 'Em".[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-70) Beyoncé also posted [co-ordinates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spatial_reference_system "Spatial reference system") to the museum on her [Instagram story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram_story "Instagram story").[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-71)
> This album has been over five years in the making. [...] It feels good to see how music can unite so many people around the world, while also amplifying the voices of some of the people who have dedicated so much of their lives educating on our [musical history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_history "Musical history"). The [criticisms I faced](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/50th_Annual_Country_Music_Association_Awards#Controversy "50th Annual Country Music Association Awards") when I first entered this genre forced me to propel past the limitations that were put on me. act ii is a result of challenging myself, and taking my time to bend and blend genres together to create this body of work. [...] I hope that you can hear my heart and soul, and all the love and passion that I poured into every detail and every sound. I focused on this album as a continuation of [RENAISSANCE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renaissance_\(Beyonc%C3%A9_album\) "Renaissance \(Beyoncé album\)")...I hope this music is an experience, creating another journey where you can close your eyes, start from the beginning and never stop. This ain't a [Country album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music"). This is a "Beyoncé" album.
— Beyoncé via Instagram in March 2024[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-pitchfork1-66)
On March 27, Beyoncé posted a graphic to Instagram of the album's tracklist inspired by vintage posters from the [Chitlin' Circuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chitlin'_Circuit "Chitlin' Circuit") era. It revealed collaborations with Dolly Parton and Willie Nelson, as well as a cover of Parton's "[Jolene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jolene "Jolene")" and the song "The Linda Martell Show". The latter song references Linda Martell, the first Black woman to achieve commercial success in the country genre.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-72)
The CD release was issued in four variants, each with a different rear cover depicting Beyoncé. It was released in Japan on March 29[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-73) and on April 12 in Europe.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-74) After the album's release, fans reported that their pre-ordered physical vinyl and CD copies were missing numerous tracks, with some asking for refunds.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-BBC_News-75)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-76)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-77)
### Levi's campaign
The American clothing company [Levi Strauss & Co.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levi_Strauss_&_Co. "Levi Strauss & Co.") saw an opportunity to better market their brand to a female audience after their product inspired the _Cowboy Carter_ track "[Levii's Jeans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levii's_Jeans "Levii's Jeans")". On September 30, 2024, the brand announced a global campaign with Beyoncé titled "Reiimagine" that stretched to August 2025. It was based on women's history with the brand and split into four reimagined historical Levi's commercials as "chapters", the first being of the company's 1985 "Laundrette" television spot, the second being 1991's "Pool Hall," the third being 1988's "Refrigerator" and the fourth being a compilation of all three entitled "The Denim Cowboy." It renamed the chapters to "The Ice", "The Heat", and "The Smoke", and had additional footage of Beyoncé entering "Laundrette" on a horse and exiting "Pool Hall" on a motorcycle.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-78)
Levi's described the partnership as "the biggest one [they've] ever done," and used Beyoncé's impact to help boost sales to $2 billion.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-79) The first commercial starring Beyoncé amassed 2.4 billion impressions in under a month.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-80) As of August 2025, three of the looks featured in the second "chapter" rank as Levi's top sellers in Europe.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-81)
### Live performances
Main articles: [Beyoncé 2024 NFL Halftime Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyonc%C3%A9_2024_NFL_Halftime_Show "Beyoncé 2024 NFL Halftime Show") and [Cowboy Carter Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter_Tour "Cowboy Carter Tour")
On November 17, 2024, it was revealed that Beyoncé would perform [a _Cowboy Carter_ medley as a halftime show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyonc%C3%A9_2024_NFL_Halftime_Show "Beyoncé 2024 NFL Halftime Show") of the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL) match game between the [Houston Texans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Texans "Houston Texans") and the [Baltimore Ravens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_Ravens "Baltimore Ravens") during Christmas Day, with the event being available on [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix").[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-82) After the broadcast performance, Beyoncé tweeted a short video clip with the caption "Look at that horse" and a stated date for January 14, 2025, within the visualizer, which led to speculations about a promotional concert tour for the album.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-83) Nevertheless, the [Cowboy Carter Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter_Tour "Cowboy Carter Tour") was officially announced on the late night of February 1, 2025, while 22 initial dates across the US, England and France were revealed on February 2.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-84)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-85)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-86)
## Cover artwork and title
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3b/Presentation_of_the_colors_at_the_Star_of_Texas_Fair_and_Rodeo%2C_produced_by_Rodeo_Austin_in_Austin%2C_Texas_LCCN2015630169.jpg/250px-Presentation_of_the_colors_at_the_Star_of_Texas_Fair_and_Rodeo%2C_produced_by_Rodeo_Austin_in_Austin%2C_Texas_LCCN2015630169.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Presentation_of_the_colors_at_the_Star_of_Texas_Fair_and_Rodeo,_produced_by_Rodeo_Austin_in_Austin,_Texas_LCCN2015630169.jpg)A horsewoman presenting the American flag at a Texas rodeo
The _Cowboy Carter_ album cover was shot by Blair Caldwell, a Los Angeles-based photographer who is from Texas. Much like the cover for _Renaissance_ —which saw Beyoncé sitting atop a stationary [disco ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disco_ball "Disco ball") horse—the _Cowboy Carter_ artwork sees Beyoncé atop a [gray horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gray_horse "Gray horse") at a [gallop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gallop "Gallop"). She rides the horse while sitting sideways (historically, [sidesaddle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sidesaddle "Sidesaddle") riding was associated with high-status women), dressed in red, white and blue clothing, wearing a cowboy hat and a sash reading "Cowboy Carter". She holds the horse's reins in one hand and a large American flag in the other.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Benzine-2024-87) The imagery is reminiscent of [rodeo queens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodeo_queen "Rodeo queen"),[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-The_Styles_Desk-2024-88) who often are asked to carry the American flag in a rodeo [grand entry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_entry "Grand entry").[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-89)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-90)
The album cover was a topic of discussion and dissection by critics. Francesca T Royster, professor at [DePaul University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DePaul_University "DePaul University") and author of _Black Country Music: Listening for Revolutions_ , wrote: "The aesthetic choice is bold and seems to be signaling the ways that Beyoncé is putting herself into conversations about nationalism, a theme very much central to discourses about country music, patriotism and authenticity, from the times of its origins."[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Demopoulos-2024-91) Critics suggested a variety of inspirations and allusions for the cover, including [presidential portraits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portraits_of_presidents_of_the_United_States "Portraits of presidents of the United States"), [Jacques-Louis David](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques-Louis_David "Jacques-Louis David")'s _[Napoleon Crossing the Alps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleon_Crossing_the_Alps "Napoleon Crossing the Alps")_ (1801–1805), [Marina Abramović](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marina_Abramovi%C4%87 "Marina Abramović")'s _The Hero_ (2001),[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Benzine-2024-87) [Kehinde Wiley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kehinde_Wiley "Kehinde Wiley")'s _Equestrian Portrait of King Philip II (Michael Jackson)_ (2009), the [Bill Pickett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Pickett "Bill Pickett") Invitational Rodeo,[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Demopoulos-2024-91) and [Eadweard Muybridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eadweard_Muybridge "Eadweard Muybridge")'s _[The Horse in Motion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Horse_in_Motion "The Horse in Motion")_ (1878).[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-The_Styles_Desk-2024-88)
The album is titled after a character "Cowboy Carter", who is inspired by the original [Black cowboys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_cowboys "Black cowboys") of the American West.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-92) Beyoncé explained: "The word cowboy itself was used in a derogatory way to describe the former slaves as 'boys', who were the most skilled and had the hardest jobs of handling horses and cattle, alike. In destroying the negative connotation, what remains is the strength and resiliency of these men who were the true definition of Western fortitude."[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Beyonc%C3%A9_Releases_Cowboy_Carter-20)

_Cowboy Carter_ was met with critical acclaim upon release, with some describing it as a "masterpiece".[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-109) Critics praised Beyoncé's blending of diverse musical genres and vocal performance, and described the album as both a grand political statement and a personal ode to Beyoncé's roots.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Nanji-2024-49)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-110)[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-111)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-112) On the review aggregator website [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), the album received a [weighted average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weighted_arithmetic_mean "Weighted arithmetic mean") score of 91 from 100 based on 22 reviews, indicating "universal acclaim".[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-mc-94)
Critics lauded _Cowboy Carter_ as an exploration and reinvention of [Americana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Americana "Americana"), as well as a celebration of Black southern culture and its contribution to the country music genre. _[The Atlantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Atlantic "The Atlantic")_ 's Spencer Kornhaber and the _[Evening Standard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evening_Standard "Evening Standard")_ 's Gemma Samways noted that the album experiments with the touchstones and musical traditions of country and Americana in order to explore its Black cultural roots.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-113)[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Samways-2024-114) Maria Sherman of the [Associated Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Press "Associated Press") wrote that the "eclectic" and "epic" album "redefines American style" and requires close examination of its references, themes and messages for full enjoyment.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-115) _[HipHopDX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HipHopDX "HipHopDX")_ 's Tai Saint-Louis described the album as a reclamation of both the "deep roots from which Beyoncé has crafted her artistry" and "the many branches that have sprouted from Black music in America".[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-116) _[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_\(magazine\) "Variety \(magazine\)")_ 's chief music critic Chris Willman characterized the album as a "piece of [agitprop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agitprop "Agitprop") and socially significant performance art" that both reflects and impacts the history of Black music and country.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-117)
Critics commended the album for what they described as its ambitious experimentation with genres, with Beyoncé reimagining country music in her image.[[d]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-121) [Neil McCormick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_McCormick "Neil McCormick") of _[The Daily Telegraph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Daily_Telegraph "The Daily Telegraph")_ felt the album pushed the boundaries of genres and mixed diverse musical styles as a polemic against the conservatism of the country genre.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-TheDailyTelegraph-97) _[Clash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clash_\(magazine\) "Clash \(magazine\)")_ and _Billboard_ characterized the album as an [ethnomusicological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethnomusicological "Ethnomusicological") study that venerates the breadth of musical subcultures of the American South,[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Clash-96)[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-122) while _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")_ critic [Ben Sisario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Sisario "Ben Sisario") described the album as a "broad essay" both on [popular music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_music "Popular music") and on genre as a concept.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-123) _[The Morning Herald")_ 's Robert Moran opined that Beyoncé's genre experimentation is in the service of celebrating the overlooked pioneers of country music while spotlighting up-and-coming Black musicians.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Moran-2024-35)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-TheIndependent-98) [Robert Christgau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Christgau "Robert Christgau") said that, while the quality of the songwriting diminishes slightly toward the end, _Cowboy Carter_ 's confident and "impressive variety" shows Beyoncé to be "our greatest female pop singer", as well as a "pretty darn good songwriter", with a considerable stake in the country sphere.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-xgau-36)
Many critics praised the album's "ambitious" scope and "cinematic" grandiosity, likening it to a [Western epic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_film "Western film").[[e]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-129) The _[Financial Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_Times "Financial Times")_ 's Ludovic Hunter-Tilney compared the epic"), with its "impressive, very American aura of importance" and "the sense that history is not only being told but also made".[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Financial_Times-126) [NPR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NPR "NPR")'s Sidney Madden equated each of the tracks to a "full-length history.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-130) Writing for the roots music journal _[No Depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Depression_\(magazine\) "No Depression \(magazine\)")_ , John Amen commented, "While 2022's _Renaissance_ spotlighted [Beyoncé] as a global MC throwing the party of the decade, _Cowboy Carter_ , framed as _Renaissance_ 's Act II, paints her as a torchbearer and synthesist, an auteur equally adept at playing the archivist and the cultural midwife".[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-131) Some critics felt that the album would fare better if it were split by musical style.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-thetimes-37) [Alexis better as a double-disc, "its wild lurches into [eclecticism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eclecticism_in_music "Eclecticism in music") are the point" and demonstrates Beyoncé's "impressive" ability to "bend musical styles to her will".[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-TheGuardian-39)

## Accolades
See also: [58th Annual Country Music Association Awards § Controversy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/58th_Annual_Country_Music_Association_Awards#Controversy "58th Annual Country Music Association Awards")
_Cowboy Carter_ earned the most nominations at the [67th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "67th Annual Grammy Awards"), with 11 nominations across multiple genres, including pop, country, Americana and melodic rap.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-173) It is the [third-most nominated album in Grammy history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_milestones#Most_nominated_albums "Grammy Award milestones"), behind [Michael Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jackson "Michael Jackson")'s _[Thriller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thriller_\(album\) "Thriller \(album\)")_ (1982) and [Quincy Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quincy_Jones "Quincy Jones")' _[The Dude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dude_\(Quincy_Jones_album\) "The Dude \(Quincy Jones album\)")_ (1981), and the most nominated album by a woman.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-174) Additionally, _Cowboy Carter_ increased Beyoncé's career total nominations to 99, breaking her tie with Jay-Z to become the [most nominated artist of all time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_milestones#Most_Grammy_nominations "Grammy Award milestones").[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-175) She joined [Kendrick Lamar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kendrick_Lamar "Kendrick Lamar") and [Jon Batiste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Batiste "Jon Batiste") as the artists who received the [third-most nominations in one night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_milestones#Most_nominations_in_one_night "Grammy Award milestones").[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-176) [The Recording Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Recording_Academy "The Recording Academy") CEO [Harvey Mason Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvey_Mason_Jr. "Harvey Mason Jr.") declared _Cowboy Carter_ 's broad nominations as a "really impressive" feat, explaining that because Grammy voters are limited to voting in particular fields, Beyoncé's nominations across genres shows that "totally different subsets of voters all really resonated with the music".[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-177) The album won [Best Country Duo/Group Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Country_Duo/Group_Performance "Best Country Duo/Group Performance") for "[II Most Wanted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/II_Most_Wanted "II Most Wanted")", [Best Country Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Country_Album "Best Country Album") and [Album of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year").[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-178)
_Cowboy Carter_ did not receive any nominations at the [58th Annual Country Music Association Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/58th_Annual_Country_Music_Association_Awards "58th Annual Country Music Association Awards").[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Romano-2024-179)[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-180)[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-181) Several publications attributed this to [conservatism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservatism_in_the_United_States "Conservatism in the United States") and [racism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racism_in_the_United_States "Racism in the United States") against Black artists in the country music industry.[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-182)[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-183)[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Romano-2024-179) _Cowboy Carter_ collaborator [Shaboozey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaboozey "Shaboozey"), who received his first two CMA Awards nominations, expressed his gratitude for Beyoncé following the lack of nominations, writing: "Thank you Beyoncé for opening a door for us, starting a conversation, and giving us one of the most innovative country albums of all time".[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Atkinson-2024-184) _Cowboy Carter_ involved artist [Dolly Parton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolly_Parton "Dolly Parton") spoke on Beyonce's apparent snub, "She's a country girl in Texas and Louisiana, so she grew up with that base. It wasn't like she just appeared out of nowhere [...] There's so many wonderful country artists that, I guess probably the country music field, they probably thought, well, we can't really leave out some of the ones that spend their whole life doing that [...] I think it was just more of what the country charts and the country artists were doing, that do that all the time, not just a specialty album."[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-185)
Despite winning Best Country Album at the Grammy on February 2, 2025, _Cowboy Carter_ also did not receive any nominations at the [60th Academy of Country Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/60th_Academy_of_Country_Music_Awards "60th Academy of Country Music Awards") on the ceremony nominations annuncement on March 27, 2026.[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-186) As happened at the 2024 CMA Awards, publications attributed this to conservatism and racism in the country music industry.[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-187)

## Commercial performance
### Streaming
_Cowboy Carter_ landed Beyoncé her biggest streaming week ever and broke streaming records on several platforms.[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-195)[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Caulfield-2024-196) On [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify"), the album became one of the most-streamed albums in a single day in 2024, the biggest debut of the year for a country album, and the biggest debut ever for any album by a Black woman, with over 76 million streams globally in its first day.[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-197)[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-198) _Cowboy Carter_ also marks the most first-day streams for a country album by a female artist in the history of [Amazon Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Music "Amazon Music").[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-BB-SpotifyRecord-199)
### United States
_Cowboy Carter_ also broke several chart records.[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-200) In the United States, _Cowboy Carter_ debuted at number one on the [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200"), with 407,000 [album-equivalent units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Album-equivalent_unit "Album-equivalent unit"). In doing so, Beyoncé became the first woman and second artist overall to debut her first eight albums at number one. _Cowboy Carter_ debuted at number one on the [Americana/Folk Albums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Americana/Folk_Albums "Americana/Folk Albums"), and [Top Country Albums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top_Country_Albums "Top Country Albums") charts, making Beyoncé the first Black woman to have a number-one country album.[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Caulfield-2024-196) The album remained atop the _Billboard_ 200 for two weeks, her first multi-week number one since 2013's _[Beyoncé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyonc%C3%A9_\(album\) "Beyoncé \(album\)")_.[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-201) With all 23 eligible songs on _Cowboy Carter_ debuting on the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), Beyoncé became the first artist to have every song on three consecutive albums chart on the _Billboard_ Hot 100. The album gave African-American country artists Martell, Adell, Kennedy, Roberts, Spencer, Jones and [Shaboozey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaboozey "Shaboozey") their first chart entries and brought Beyoncé's career total Hot 100 entries to 106, the [third highest for a female artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_100_chart_achievements_and_milestones#Most_Hot_100_entries "List of Billboard Hot 100 chart achievements and milestones").[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-202) Beyoncé also topped eighteen [_Billboard_ charts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_charts "Billboard charts") the week of _Cowboy Carter_ 's release, including the [Artist 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artist_100 "Artist 100"), Hot 100 Songwriters and Hot 100 Producers; she also became the first artist to simultaneously hold the number one positions on both the Top Country Albums and the [_Billboard_ Dance/Electronic Albums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance/Electronic_Albums "Dance/Electronic Albums") charts, with [_Renaissance_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renaissance_\(Beyonc%C3%A9_album\) "Renaissance \(Beyoncé album\)") atop the latter.[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-203) _Cowboy Carter_ has spent over 50 weeks on the _Billboard_ 200, making Beyoncé the Black woman with the most albums to chart 50 or more weeks, surpassing [Whitney Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitney_Houston "Whitney Houston") and [Mariah Carey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mariah_Carey "Mariah Carey") with a total of eight.
### Internationally
By its fourth day of release, _Cowboy Carter_ was outselling the rest of the week's top five bestselling albums combined in the UK.[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-204) The album debuted at number one on the [UK Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Albums_Chart "UK Albums Chart") selling 40,000 copies in its first week.[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-205) This became Beyoncé's fifth album to do so as a solo act, and her sixth including [Destiny's Child](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Destiny's_Child "Destiny's Child")'s discography. The album also debuted at number one on the [Official Vinyl Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Official_Vinyl_Albums_Chart "Official Vinyl Albums Chart") and has spent eight consecutive weeks at number one on the [UK Country Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UK_Country_Albums_Chart_number_ones_of_2024 "List of UK Country Albums Chart number ones of 2024"), becoming the first album by an African American female artist to reach the top spot on that chart. With "[Texas Hold 'Em](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Hold_'Em_\(song\) "Texas Hold 'Em \(song\)")" returning to number one on the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart") concurrently with the album's release, Beyoncé topped both charts simultaneously for the first time since _[Dangerously in Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dangerously_in_Love "Dangerously in Love")_ and "[Crazy in Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crazy_in_Love "Crazy in Love")" did so in 2003.[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-BB-SpotifyRecord-199) Beyoncé also became the first Black artist to top the UK Charts with a country album and the first artist to simultaneously top the Album Chart and Singles Charts with a country album and a country single.[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-206)
In Canada, the album debuted at number one on the [Canadian Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Albums_Chart "Canadian Albums Chart"), becoming Beyoncé's fifth album to achieve this as well as her tenth top-ten project in the country. Twenty out of 23 eligible songs on _Cowboy Carter_ debuted on the [Canadian Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Hot_100 "Canadian Hot 100"), giving African-American country artists Martell, Adell, Kennedy, Roberts, Spencer, Jones and [Shaboozey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaboozey "Shaboozey") their first chart entries and bringing Beyoncé's career total Canadian Hot 100 entries to 84.[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-207)[_[failed verification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_]
In Australia, the album debuted at number one on the [ARIA Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ARIA_Albums_Chart "ARIA Albums Chart"), becoming the singer's fourth consecutive project to achieve this since [_Beyoncé_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyonc%C3%A9_\(album\) "Beyoncé \(album\)") (2013). It also became the first country-genre album by a female artist to top the chart since 2017, when the top position was occupied by [Shania Twain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shania_Twain "Shania Twain")'s [_Now_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Now_\(Shania_Twain_album\) "Now \(Shania Twain album\)").[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-208) The album remained atop the ARIA Chart for two consecutive weeks.[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-209)
In Germany, the album debuted atop the [German Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Albums_Chart "German Albums Chart"), becoming Beyoncé's first number one album as a solo artist since _[Dangerously in Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dangerously_in_Love "Dangerously in Love")_ topped the chart in 2003.[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-210)
## Cultural and societal impact
Upon release, _Cowboy Carter_ had a significant impact on music, fashion, business and culture, with Stevie Wonder and _Variety_ 's Chris Willman suggesting it may be the most-discussed album of the 21st century.[[f]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-216) _Cowboy Carter_ was widely discussed in the media following its release, with all major news networks broadcasting features exploring the impact of the album.[[g]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-221) [CNN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN "CNN") released a documentary on [Max](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_\(streaming_service\) "Max \(streaming service\)") titled _Call Me Country: Beyoncé & Nashville's Renaissance_, which explores the album's impact on the country music landscape and the inclusion of Black artists within the genre.[[215]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-222) An episode of _[Nightline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nightline "Nightline")_ focused on the album and its impact on the country music space.[[216]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-223)
### Country music
_Cowboy Carter_ increased the listenership of country music and made it more accessible to new audiences, with publications describing it as "a cultural shift", "a watershed moment" and "a tipping point" in the genre's history.[[h]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-228) The album drove over 36 million people to stream country music for the first time on [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify").[[221]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-229) The album was credited by _The Times_ as making country music become mainstream in the UK,[[222]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-230) with one survey finding that 60% of British respondents started listening to country music following the release of _Cowboy Carter_.[[223]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Jarvis-2024-231) In Sweden, the number of people listening to country music increased by 60% following the release of the album, which is the largest increase for any genre in Swedish history.[[224]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-232) A worldwide study found that over one-third of Gen Z respondents began listening to country music after Beyoncé entered the genre.[[225]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-233) There was a 38% increase in views of country music videos globally on [Vevo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vevo "Vevo") following the album's release, as well as a 40% increase in Black 18–34-year-olds listening to country radio.[[226]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-234) _Cowboy Carter_ was said to redefine what it means to be a country artist, with Emi Tuyetnhi Tran from [NBC News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC_News "NBC News") commenting that it will "open the floodgates" for other country musicians.[[220]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-BBC_News-2024-227)[[227]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Tran-2024-235) _Cowboy Carter_ sparked discourse on the boundaries of the country music genre and its roots within Black music, and drove cultural conversations on the inclusion of Black artists within the genre.[[i]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-240)
#### Country artists
_Cowboy Carter_ boosted the careers of rising country acts.[[232]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-241) In _The Tennessean_ , Andrea Williams wrote that Beyoncé opened the door for others in country music, proving Black songwriters, producers and musicians belong in the genre.[[233]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-242) NPR's Amanda Marie Martínez wrote that the album revealed the "strong demand" for country music made by Black artists and a "growing community" of Black country fans.[[227]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Tran-2024-235)
After featuring on the album, [Shaboozey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaboozey "Shaboozey") advanced the release of his single "[A Bar Song (Tipsy)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Bar_Song_\(Tipsy\) "A Bar Song \(Tipsy\)")" to take advantage of his increased visibility. The song would peak at number 1 on the _Billboard_ Hot 100 and _Billboard_ Hot Country Songs, replacing Beyoncé's own "Texas Hold 'Em", becoming the first time in history that two Black artists led the latter chart back to back.[[234]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-243) Shaboozey thanked Beyoncé for "changing [his] life" and "opening a door for us".[[235]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-244)[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Atkinson-2024-184)
[Linda Martell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linda_Martell "Linda Martell"), who was the first commercially successful Black female country artist, saw a 127,430 percent increase in streams of her music after twice appearing on the album.[[236]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-245) In 2025, "[Color Him Father](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Color_Him_Father#Linda_Martell_version "Color Him Father")", her 1969 breakthrough record, was inducted into the [Grammy Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Hall_of_Fame "Grammy Hall of Fame") as a result of the increased recognition in her catalog.[[237]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-246)
Other Black female country musicians also saw a significant increase in streams due to the album, such as [Reyna Roberts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reyna_Roberts "Reyna Roberts") (250%), [Rissi Palmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rissi_Palmer "Rissi Palmer") (110%), [Tanner Adell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanner_Adell "Tanner Adell") (188%) and [K. Michelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K._Michelle "K. Michelle") (185%),[[238]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-247) while [Adia Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adia_Victoria "Adia Victoria"), [Amira Unplugged](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amira_Unplugged "Amira Unplugged"), [Brittney Spencer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brittney_Spencer "Brittney Spencer"), [Mickey Guyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mickey_Guyton "Mickey Guyton"), [Tiera Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiera_Kennedy "Tiera Kennedy"), Rhiannon Giddens and [Sacha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacha_\(singer\) "Sacha \(singer\)") also saw increases in their music sales. Black-led country organizations such as the [Black Opry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Opry "Black Opry") also received a significant increase in followers.[[239]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-248)

### Fashion and lifestyle
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/61/Cowboy_Hats.jpg/250px-Cowboy_Hats.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cowboy_Hats.jpg)_Cowboy Carter_ made [Western wear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_wear "Western wear") a defining fashion trend for 2024 and led to a 326% surge in sales of [cowboy hats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_hat "Cowboy hat").
Beyoncé's embrace of country music and culture ignited fashion trends and boosted sales of [Western wear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_wear "Western wear").[[267]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-276)[[268]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-277)[[269]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-278) _Cowboy Carter_ helped transform cowboy fashion and aesthetics from a "caricature" into a "staple of the modern wardrobe" according to _Vogue_ ,[[270]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-279) while [Vanessa Friedman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Friedman "Vanessa Friedman"), fashion director and chief fashion critic at _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")_ , wrote that Beyoncé has shifted the industry by mainstreaming Western aesthetics and determining the "look of the moment".[[271]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Friedman-2024-280) _Cowboy Carter_ led to a surge in interest in Western clothing, including an increase in searches for Western-style jeans (610%), bolo ties (566%), flared denim (372%), cowboy boots (224%) and cowboy hats (213%).[[271]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Friedman-2024-280)[[272]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-281)[[273]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-282)[[274]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-283) Hat brand [Stetson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stetson "Stetson") reported an increase in interest in their products following Beyoncé's embrace of Western lifestyle.[[275]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-284)
_Cowboy Carter_ led to a 326 percent surge in sales of cowboy hats, while units sold of boots and fringed suede jackets both jumped by 45 percent.[[276]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-285)[[277]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-286) [Fast fashion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_fashion "Fast fashion") retailers such as [Forever 21](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forever_21 "Forever 21") increased the amount of Western clothing available for sale by over 300 percent due to the album.[[278]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-287) Inspired by the album, the prominence of Western and country styling within the fashion landscape increased by 45 percent.[[271]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Friedman-2024-280) The [Ralph Lauren Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Lauren_Corporation "Ralph Lauren Corporation") designer brand was inspired by the trend for their 2024 fall/winter collection.[[279]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-288) [GQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GQ "GQ")'s Editor-in-Chief [Will Welch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Welch_\(editor\) "Will Welch \(editor\)") credited _Cowboy Carter_ for inspiring the 'American Rodeo' western theme of their 29th annual Men of the Year party.[[280]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-289)
In the UK, a national survey found that 25% of respondents took up [line dancing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Line_dancing "Line dancing") and 40% started wearing Western clothing following the release of _Cowboy Carter_.[[223]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Jarvis-2024-231) Publications reported that the album aided a reclamation of country identity and [western culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_lifestyle "Western lifestyle") by Black people.[[231]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Willingham-2024-239)[[281]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-290) The album had an impact on rodeos in Canada such as the [Calgary Stampede](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calgary_Stampede "Calgary Stampede"), broadening its audience.[[282]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-291)

"Levi Strauss & Co.") experienced 20% surges in both its stock value and store footfall after Beyoncé referenced the brand on _Cowboy Carter_.
After Beyoncé referenced the American clothing company [Levi Strauss & Co.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levi_Strauss_&_Co. "Levi Strauss & Co.") on the _Cowboy Carter_ track "[Levii's Jeans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levii's_Jeans "Levii's Jeans")", the company reported a 20% boost on their [stock price](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stock_price "Stock price").[[283]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-292) The album singlehandedly generated an additional $1.2 million for the brand, from an increase of 1.5 billion impressions online.[[271]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Friedman-2024-280)[[284]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Yahoo!_Finance-2024-293) Levi's also noted a 20% rise in footfall at US stores after the release of the album, while British retailer [John Lewis & Partners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lewis_&_Partners "John Lewis & Partners") reported that searches for "women's Levi's jeans" were up 263% since the record was announced.[[285]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-294) In reference to the track name, Levi's added a second letter "i" to its name and logo on social media.[[286]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-295)[[287]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-296) Levi Strauss CFO Harmit Singh described Beyoncé as "the center of culture, the cultural czar", adding: "We are humbled and honored that she chose us to talk about our brand".[[284]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Yahoo!_Finance-2024-293)
Following the release of _Cowboy Carter_ , ridesharing company [Uber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uber "Uber") offered 16% off to riders who use the code "16CARRIAGES", a reference to a song on the album.[[288]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-297) In response, [Lyft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyft "Lyft") offered its riders 50% off with the code "SPAGHETTI24", another reference to a song on the album.[[289]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-298) Lyft also changed images of cars on its map to white horses as a reference to the _Cowboy Carter_ album cover.[[290]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-299)[[291]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-300)

### Samples, interpolations and covers
  * "Ameriican Requiem" 
    * contains excerpts from "Heart of the City (Ain't No Love)", written by [Shawn Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Carter "Shawn Carter"), Michael Price and Dan Walsh and performed by [Jay-Z](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay-Z "Jay-Z"), as well as Jay-Z's performance of the song on _[MTV Unplugged](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Unplugged_\(Jay-Z_album\) "MTV Unplugged \(Jay-Z album\)")_.
    * contains an interpolation of "[For What It's Worth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_What_It's_Worth "For What It's Worth")", written by [Stephen Stills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Stills "Stephen Stills") and performed by [Buffalo Springfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo_Springfield "Buffalo Springfield").
  * "Blackbiird" 
    * is a cover of [the Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles")' 1968 song "[Blackbird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackbird_\(Beatles_song\) "Blackbird \(Beatles song\)")", and features a sample of the instrumental from the original master recording.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Kreps-2024-53)[[294]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-303)
  * "Smoke Hour Willie Nelson" 
    * contains excerpts from "Laughing Yodel", written and performed by Charles Anderson.
    * contains excerpts from "Grinnin' in Your Face", written and performed by [Son House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Son_House "Son House").
    * contains excerpts from "[Down by the River Side](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Down_by_the_Riverside "Down by the Riverside")", written and performed by [Sister Rosetta Tharpe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sister_Rosetta_Tharpe "Sister Rosetta Tharpe").
    * contains excerpts from "[Maybellene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maybellene "Maybellene")", written and performed by [Chuck Berry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Berry "Chuck Berry").
    * contains excerpts from "[Don't Let Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Let_Go_\(Roy_Hamilton_song\) "Don't Let Go \(Roy Hamilton song\)")", written by Jesse Stone and performed by [Roy Hamilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Hamilton "Roy Hamilton").
  * "Jolene" 
    * is a cover of Dolly Parton's "[Jolene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jolene "Jolene")", with new lyrics.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Kreps-2024-53)[[295]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Horowitz-2024-304)
  * "Daughter" 
    * contains elements of Violin Concerto in D Major, Op. III No. 1: II. Adagio by [Joseph Bologne, Chevalier de Saint-Georges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Bologne,_Chevalier_de_Saint-Georges "Joseph Bologne, Chevalier de Saint-Georges").[[296]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-305)

  * "Spaghettii" 
    * contains a sample of "Aquecimento das Danadas", written and performed by O Mandrake.
  * "Ya Ya" 
    * contains excerpts from "[These Boots Are Made for Walkin'](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/These_Boots_Are_Made_for_Walkin' "These Boots Are Made for Walkin'")", written by [Lee Hazlewood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Hazlewood "Lee Hazlewood") and performed by [Nancy Sinatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Sinatra "Nancy Sinatra").
    * contains interpolation from "[Good Vibrations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_Vibrations "Good Vibrations")", written by [Brian Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Wilson "Brian Wilson") and [Mike Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Love "Mike Love") and performed by [the Beach Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beach_Boys "The Beach Boys").
  * "Oh Louisiana" 
    * contains excerpts from "Oh Louisiana", written and performed by Chuck Berry.
  * "II Hands II Heaven" 
    * contains an uncredited sample of the [Underworld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Underworld_\(band\) "Underworld \(band\)") song "[Born Slippy Nuxx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Born_Slippy_Nuxx "Born Slippy Nuxx")", written by [Rick Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Smith_\(musician\) "Rick Smith \(musician\)"), [Karl Hyde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl_Hyde "Karl Hyde") and [Darren Emerson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darren_Emerson "Darren Emerson").[[299]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-308)
  * "Sweet Honey Buckiin'" 
    * contains interpolation from "[I Fall to Pieces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Fall_to_Pieces "I Fall to Pieces")", written by [Hank Cochran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hank_Cochran "Hank Cochran") and [Harlan Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harlan_Howard "Harlan Howard") and performed by [Patsy Cline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patsy_Cline "Patsy Cline").[[295]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboy_Carter#cite_note-Horowitz-2024-304)
